title: Severe bee sting anaphylaxis at a park fun day
setting: Park fun day. 8M felt dizzy and sat down after a bee sting, now clutching his chest, gasping for air, face swollen with visible hives on skin.
verdictExplanation: Sudden onset of systemic reaction after a known trigger: airway (face/lip swelling), breathing (wheeze and stridor, rate 36/min), and circulation (hypotension 77/58, fainted). Sick: adrenaline now.

shared.response: Alert but highly distressed, level of response dropping
shared.breathing: Rapid, labored, with audible wheeze and stridor
shared.circulation: Widespread red hives over skin, tachycardic

er.exposure: Outdoors, hot sun, wearing summer clothing

history.complaint: Bee sting and severe breathing difficulty
history.history: Stung by a bee 10 minutes ago while playing in the park, developed rapid hives and swelling
history.pmh: Known severe allergy to bee stings
history.drugs: Prescribed an auto-injector (has two in the car, none on person)

followUp.question: What is the correct first-line treatment for this severe allergic reaction?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, sit him upright to ease breathing, and administer IM adrenaline if available
Give him antihistamine tablets and wait 30 minutes to see if the hives resolve
Lay him flat on his back and give him cold water to drink
Apply a cold compress to the sting site and do not give adrenaline

followUp.explanation: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening emergency. Adrenaline IM is the first-line and most critical treatment. Call 999 immediately. Either positions are fine if appropriate - given the extensive circulatory compromise, they should be lying flat with legs raised. In earlier stages, sitting against the wall in the W position (not on a chair) might be better to support breathing. Antihistamines must never delay adrenaline. Do not give oral fluids.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999. Sit upright if breathing is the main issue. Help administer his auto-injector if located.
levelFlags.erNotes: Anaphylaxis with airway and circulation involvement. Administer IM Adrenaline via their adrenaline autoinjector into the anterolateral thigh. Give high-flow oxygen, monitor SpO₂ and BP closely, and prepare for a second auto-injector if no improvement in 5 minutes.
